title: नेपालको इतिहासका स्रोतव्यक्ति युरोपेली पादरीहरुको प्रारम्भिक नेपाल प्रवेश : सामाजिक प्रभाव Nepalko Itihaska Srotbyakti Europeli Padariharuko Prarambhik Nepal Pravesh : Samajik Prabhav
authors: पोखरेल विवश Pokhrel Biwas, गोपाल Gopal
nepali: नेपालको संरचनादेखि अनवरतरुपमा आजसम्म नै यो भूभाग एक अद्भुतस्थल रहिआएको छ । यस क्षेत्रको समय–समयको सामाजिक–सांस्कृतिकलगायत पक्षमा प्रकाश पार्ने अनेक साधनमध्ये यहाँ आएका यात्रीहरुको यात्रा वृत्तान्त (टिपोट) पनि एक सहायक सामग्रीको रुपमा रहेको छ र त्यो वृत्तान्त (वयान) प्रस्तुत गर्ने यात्रीहरु स्रोतव्यक्तिको रुपमा स्थापित देखिन्छन् । यहाँ इ. सम्वत् प्रारम्भ हुनुभन्दा धेरै अगाडिदेखि नै उच्च प्रतिष्ठित व्यक्तिहरुको आगमन भइसकेकोमा दुई मत देखिदैन । विशेष गरी नेपालसंगसंगै रहेका उत्तर तथा दखिक्षणी राज्यबाट नेपालप्रवेश गर्ने क्रम इस्वी सम्वत् प्रारम्भपछि झन बढेर गयो । मध्यकाल अर्थात् इ. सोह्रौं शताब्दीको उत्तरार्धबाट भने युरोपेली इसाई धर्मालम्बी पादरीहरुको पनि नेपाल प्रवेश प्रारम्भ भयो । उनीहरुको विशेष काठमाडौं उपत्यका बसाइँले यहाँको परम्परागत सामाजिक–धार्मिक जीवनमा केही न केही प्रभाव पा¥यो । यहाँ आएका कतिपय इसाई पादरीको यात्रा वृत्तान्त तात्कालिक इतिहास–संस्कृति जानकारीको सहायक सामग्री हुनपुग्यो । यस लेखमा स्रोतव्यक्ति, उनीहरुको टिपोट तथा तात्कालिक समाजमा पु¥याएको प्रभाव आदिबारे केही न केही प्रकाश पार्ने कोशिस गरिएको छ ।
american_english: From the very formation of Nepal and continuously down to the present day, this land has remained a remarkable place. Among the many sources that shed light on the social, cultural, and other aspects of this region at different times, the travel accounts (reports) of travelers who came here also stand as a useful resource, and those travelers who presented such accounts (narratives) are seen to be established as source persons. There is no dispute that highly reputed persons had already arrived here long before the beginning of the Christian era. Especially, in addition to Nepal, the movement of people entering Nepal from the northern and southern states increased further after the beginning of the Christian era. In the medieval period, that is, from the latter half of the sixteenth century CE, the entry of European Christian missionary priests into Nepal also began. Their stay, particularly in the Kathmandu Valley, had some effect or other on the traditional social and religious life here. The travel accounts of some of the Christian priests who came here became useful materials for understanding the contemporary history and culture. In this article, an attempt has been made to shed some light on source persons, their reports, and the impact they had on the society of that time, among other things.

informal_english: Right from when Nepal was formed and all the way through to today, this place has stayed pretty amazing. Out of all the different sources that throw light on the social, cultural and other sides of this region at different times, the travel accounts (reports) of travellers who came here are also a handy resource, and the travellers who put together those accounts (narratives) are seen as source persons. There’s no two ways about it — highly reputed people had already turned up here long before the Christian era kicked off. Especially, on top of Nepal itself, more and more people started entering Nepal from the northern and southern states after the beginning of the Christian era. In the medieval period, that is, from the latter half of the sixteenth century CE, European Christian missionary priests also started coming into Nepal. Their stay, especially in the Kathmandu Valley, had some sort of impact on the traditional social and religious life here. The travel accounts of some of the Christian priests who came here ended up being useful material for getting a handle on the history and culture of the time. In this article, we’ve had a go at shedding a bit of light on these source persons, their reports, and the impact they had on the society back then, among other things.
translator_notes: The Nepali terms यात्रा वृत्तान्त (टिपोट) and वृत्तान्त (वयान) were rendered with their parenthetical glosses preserved in English as 'travel accounts (reports)' and 'accounts (narratives)' to reflect the source text. The title text embedded in the abstract field was not separately translated as it appears in metadata; the abstract body was translated in strict sentence order.
